titulo: Intera, identity and digital strategy · Roger Avellana
descripcion: Case study: visual identity and digital content strategy for Intera. Challenge, process, deliverables and results.
entradilla: Intera had grown faster than its image. First I redesigned its visual identity so that a complex technology company could present itself with a clear, consistent brand; then I took that system to social media with a steady, measurable content strategy.

resumen.reto: Each department used its own version of the logo, and social media was published without a plan: loose pieces, different tones and no data to know what worked.
resumen.solucion: A complete brand system (logo, palette, typography and templates) and, on top of it, a content strategy with an editorial calendar, post packs and a monthly metrics report.
resumen.resultado: A brand that is recognizable on every medium, and social channels that publish consistently, with the same tone and data-driven decisions.

proceso.intro: Two linked stages: first, put the identity in order; then give it a voice on social media with a system the team could maintain.

pasos.texto: Interviews with management and teams, plus a review of all materials and social channels to understand what worked and what didn’t.
A simplified logo, palette, typography and iconography, tested at full size on paper and on screen.
Content pillars, tone per channel and a monthly editorial calendar, with templates ready for every format.
A monthly metrics report with conclusions and adjustments for the following month.

entregables.titulo: One system, from the brand to the last post.
entregables.intro: Every element was designed to work with the others: the logo, the stationery, the social media templates and the editorial calendar.

cifras.texto: pieces produced with the new brand system
posts a month with an editorial calendar, up from an average of 4
social media reach in the first year of the strategy

testimonio.texto: Roger combines visual and strategic judgment in an unusual way, understanding the brand as a system rather than a collection of loose pieces.
